* Doctoral researcher at University of Jena
* Author and maintainer of `mlts` package, working mostly on pre-processing functions
* Research areas: latent state-trait theory, causality, time-varying confounding in panel and intensive longitudinal data

## Get to the Material


### Get the workshop materials from our workshop Github:

#### With package `usethis` (recommended)

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

install.packages("usethis")
usethis::create_from_github("https://github.com/KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_SAA2026")
```

* This should download the workshop directory and open the R project file directly


#### Or download the Github project as ZIP file:

1. Open the link: [https://github.com/KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_SAA2026](https://github.com/KennethKoslowski/mlts_workshop_SAA2026)
2. Click the green Code button, then Download ZIP
3. Extract the ZIP file
4. Open the `SAA_2026_html.Rproj` file by clicking it (it should open in a new R session)


---

## Things to Prepare for the Workshop

#### Quick overview of the workshop directory

The workshop directory from Github contains all the workshop materials.

* Follow the slides by opening `index.html` in the main directory in your browser
* The directory `live_session` contains scripts (and solutions) for the hands-on session exercises. You can directly work within the script or create them yourself!

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width = "45%"}

#### Required packages

* For following along all the examples by yourself, you need the current development version of `mlts`
* We prepared the R script `install_packages.R` in the directory `live_session`. Please run it once by opening it and running all lines of code or copy in the R console:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

source("./live_session/install_packages.R")
```

* If you are asked to install updates, click yes to all. It might take a few minutes!

:::

::: {.column width = "5%"}
:::

::: {.column width = "45%"}
#### Data

* We use data from a study by @Bolzenkoetter2024 (openly available)
* To get the data locally, please run the script `bolzen_prepare.R` in the directory `live_session`:

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| eval: false

source("./live_session/bolzen_prepare.R")
```

* This will generate data files in a directory called `downloaded_data`

:::
::::
